items.title: Richard Brunies Interview, 1959-04-27
items.q: And a fellow by the name of Big Boy. And a piano. ... And we used to have a big bus. I used to travel from one place to the other.

ctx.x: And we share, we didn't have, how was it, Stump? We had drums, vocalizers. And, uh, oh, I can't think of anything. He's driving on banjo. I don't know even. And a fellow by the name of Big Boy. And a piano. Girl goes on piano. And we used to have a big bus. I used to travel from one place to the other. Especially when the colleges, the schools, you see. You get in front of a drugstore, pull out a piano, a piece and stuff, a plane, and it's all those girls coming from different places, you know. And, uh, we'd…

Did you ever use piano much in the early bands? Oh, yeah. I had a piano a lot of times. Yeah. Well, I don't want to bother you anymore. We've been having a nice talk here. I don't want to keep asking you a lot of questions. I can't think of much more. I can't think of much more, actually, to ask you. I wondered if there was any more about the early music, the very first that you heard the kind of parades, even when you were a boy, before you learned to play. Did they have the parades?
